title.title: Exponential state costs for two-way automata
title.subtitle: Claim: two-way deterministic automata need exponentially many states to simulate one-way nondeterministic ones

plain: A reading machine that can move back and forth needs vastly more memory states to replace guessing

beats.text: Sakoda–Sipser's liveness language on $h$ points: a one-way NFA needs $h + 3$ states
Claimed: any $s$-state two-way DFA for it has $4(s+2)^2 \ge 2^{\lfloor (h-2)/31 \rfloor}$
Exponential overtakes linear; with the paper's constant 31 it takes a while

steps: Record how the machine enters and leaves each cell
Those records pair up ports, like a matching
Matchings with few ports cannot track all the guessing

data.label: a matching of ports per cell

achievement.label: Sakoda–Sipser question (1978), growing alphabets
achievement.context: Before: only quadratic lower bounds for unrestricted two-way DFAs
achievement.note: Hard inputs are long, so no L/poly versus NL separation is claimed

verify.detail: Complementation, determinization and liveness: all three statements in Lean
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: Can a machine reading back and forth replace guessing cheaply? Asked in nineteen seventy eight.
Its visits to each cell form matchings, which cannot track all the guessing.

sources.quote: One-way liveness on h points has an (h+3)-state one-way NFA but every equivalent s-state 2DFA has 4(s+2)^2 >= 2^{floor((h-2)/31)}
Sakoda-Sipser (STOC 1978) asked whether 2NFA/1NFA -> 2DFA needs exponentially many states
and for unrestricted ones only quadratic bounds
this cannot be such a bound, and no complexity-class consequence is claimed
main theorem formalized: TwoWayComplementation.lean, TwoWayDeterminization.lean, OneWayLiveness.lean; standard axioms
